name: ema_crossover_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, EMA(12)/(36) crossovers in range-bound intraday sessions attract late retail algo entries at precisely the moment the 60-90 second price impulse has exhausted — the crossover fires 1-2 minutes after the directional move began. When NIFTY's current 5-minute ATR is below 1.3× the 30-minute ATR baseline (range-bound regime), these crossover chasers create predictable supply/demand imbalance on the wrong side of an over-extended move. The 10-second confirmation wait (2 bars for price to cross back through the slow EMA) distinguishes genuine reversions from breakouts: if NIFTY is truly trending, it will NOT recross the slow EMA within 2 bars of the crossover, so only clean fade setups pass.

indicators.name: ema_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute fast EMA. NOT 108 bars (9 × 12 blind scaling). We trade the fast reversion within 30-90 seconds of the crossover, so the trigger EMA must be 1-minute scale. A 9-minute EMA (original period at 1-min bars) at 5s resolution would be 108 bars — far too slow for a 90-second hold. We want to detect the micro-crossover that retail algos react to, which occurs over 60-second momentum bursts on NIFTY.

indicators.name: ema_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute slow EMA. NOT 252 bars (21 × 12). The slow EMA defines the trend being faded. At 30-90s hold time, 3 minutes of context is sufficient to define a short-term trend direction on NIFTY. Longer periods (21-min equivalent) would make the crossover fire too rarely and miss intraday regime transitions. The 3:1 ratio to the fast EMA matches the original 9:21 ratio.

indicators.name: atr_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute ATR measuring current NIFTY volatility. Compressed from the original's 60-bar 1-min ATR (= 60 minutes) to 60-bar 5s ATR (= 5 minutes) because we need same-horizon volatility assessment matching our trade timescale. A 5-minute ATR captures whether current price action is choppy or expansive — the relevant regime for a 30-90 second fade.

indicators.name: atr_baseline
indicators.purpose: 30-minute rolling mean of the 5-min ATR, serving as the intraday volatility baseline. Replaces the original's 1950-bar weekly ATR median — the same conceptual filter (is current ATR elevated vs normal?) adapted to intraday availability. 360 bars = 30 minutes provides enough history to define 'normal' session ATR while resetting each day and capturing session regime shifts.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP from 09:15. Cumulative measure — no scaling needed. Used as directional extension filter: bullish crossover is only faded when NIFTY was above VWAP at crossover time (long side over-extended), bearish crossover only faded when below VWAP. This ensures we only fade moves that overshot the institutional benchmark level.

conditions: EMA(12) crossed above EMA(36) exactly 2 bars ago (10 seconds ago)
close[now] < ema_36[now] (price has already recrossed back below slow EMA — reversion confirmed)
close[crossover_bar] > vwap[crossover_bar] * 1.001 (bullish crossover fired from above-VWAP position — over-extension)
atr_60 < atr_ratio_threshold * atr_baseline (range-bound regime, not trending)
buy_pe.confirmation: Price must recross slow EMA within 2 bars (10s) of the crossover firing — confirms it was a failed breakout, not a genuine trend start

conditions: EMA(12) crossed below EMA(36) exactly 2 bars ago (10 seconds ago)
close[now] > ema_36[now] (price has recrossed back above slow EMA — reversion confirmed)
close[crossover_bar] < vwap[crossover_bar] * 0.999 (bearish crossover fired from below-VWAP position — over-extension to downside)
buy_ce.confirmation: Price must recross slow EMA within 10s — same logic as PE entry

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option pts = ~8 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5. In range-bound conditions, a failed EMA fade that moves 8 spot pts against us signals a genuine breakout (not a range reversal), and we exit. Typical range-bound NIFTY moves are 5-12 spot pts; an 8-pt adverse move exhausts the expected range and invalidates the thesis.
exit.target_rationale: 6 option pts = ~12 NIFTY spot pts. Range-bound NIFTY crossover fades revert 12-20 spot pts back toward VWAP within 90 seconds based on typical intraday range structure. Targeting the lower bound (12 pts × 0.5 delta = 6 option pts) at 1:1.5 risk:reward provides margin for slippage while remaining achievable within the time stop.

filters.vix_filter: none — range-bound ATR filter handles volatility regime
filters.time_filter: no trades before 09:25 (skip pre-open noise) or after 15:20
filters.volume_filter: none — index volume at 5s resolution is too noisy to be reliable
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — retail EMA crossover algos are still prevalent in Indian markets but gradually declining; the range-bound filter ensures we only trade when the behavioral edge is most reliable

adaptation_notes: Four key changes from original: (1) EMA periods compressed to 12/36 bars (1-min/3-min) from 9/21 minutes — we catch the fast 30-90s reversion, not the 5-25 minute recovery. (2) ATR regime filter scaled to 5-minute current vs 30-minute baseline, replacing the original's weekly-median calculation — same concept (is ATR elevated?) with intraday data. (3) Removed volume filter — NIFTY volume at 5s is too noisy; VWAP position replaces it as the extension confirmation. (4) Kept the 2-bar wait for confirmation, which maps to exactly 10 seconds at 5s resolution (vs 2 minutes in original) — the principle is identical, only the absolute time differs.
weaknesses: In genuine NIFTY breakout days (budget, RBI decisions, US market moves), the range filter may admit trades that then run against us significantly
The 2-bar (10-second) confirmation is very tight — 5s NIFTY bars have high noise, a single noisy bar could trigger a false confirmation
EMA(12) and EMA(36) have only 60s and 180s of history — may be sensitive to very short-term NIFTY spike/reversal patterns not related to the behavioral thesis
